subject: Standby Entitlement & EU edge: amendment request for renewal
messages:
From: Claire O'Neill <claire@medsilo.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Standby entitlement for renewal — EU residency + APAC burst

Hi Mina,

As we're preparing to sign the renewal later this quarter, we want to add a formal standby/standby-entitlement for EU edge capacity and an APAC warm-standby for cross-region failover. Two asks from our side:

1) Add an "EU Edge Standby" entitlement so we have reserved cold-standby capacity in the EU (to satisfy our data residency requirement for primary traffic). This will be idle unless our primary node degrades.
2) Add APAC warm-standby (replicated models + KV sync) to cover regional surges and cross-region failover testing windows.

High-level numbers: target committed CPU/GPU equivalent: ~2 cards in EU (for baseline), warm-standby in APAC able to handle 30% of peak QPS within 10 minutes. We can provide signature traffic profiles if useful.

Questions:
- How does Redwood bill standby capacity vs active dedicated?
- What change to SLA/credits when failover is exercised?
- Can you provide evidence of EU data residency controls and audit logs for compliance review (SOC2 snapshot or equivalent)?

We want this captured as an amendment to the renewal (12-months preferred) rather than a separate SOW if possible. If there are commercial constraints, please flag.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

— Claire
Claire O'Neill
Head of Platform Ops, MedSilo

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Claire O'Neill <claire@medsilo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby entitlement for renewal — EU residency + APAC burst

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we can structure this as an amendment to the renewal and offer two paths (reserved EU standby + APAC warm-standby) with explicit failover playbooks and billing rules.

Proposal (high level):
- Add an "EU Standby Entitlement" line item: reserved capacity in EU (idle) with monthly reservation fee at 40% of the equivalent active dedicated price. Activation during a failover window converts it to active at the standard rate (with credits for downtime per the SLA).
- APAC Warm-Standby: replicated model instances and KV sync running at reduced capacity to allow 10-minute warm-up to 30% peak QPS. Billed as a lower-capacity reservation (25% of active) + short activation delta.
- Term: align with your renewal (12 months).
- Operational items: scheduled quarterly failover drills, pre-agreed failover test windows, and an automated telemetry handoff (tracing + token-level logs).

Attachments: I'm attaching a draft amendment + a quick pricing spreadsheet to start (standby_entitlement_draft.pdf, capacity_pricing.xlsx). Please review and we'll iterate.

Next steps:
1) If this fits commercially, Ben can produce a redline-ready amendment and pricing anchor.
2) Security questions (SOC2, audit logs): our security team can provide scoped evidence and an audit runbook; I'll loop in Legal & Security if you confirm.
3) Schedule a 30-min alignment call to lock numbers and test-window dates.

If helpful, propose Wed 9/22 9:00am PT for a call.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire O'Neill <claire@medsilo.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby entitlement for renewal — commercial options

Claire — following Mina's note, here are two commercial options for the amendment. Numbers are illustrative; we'll finalize after you confirm the committed baseline traffic profile.

Option A (Preferred):
- EU Standby: 2x reserved instance-equivalents (idle) — reservation fee = $18,000/month (40% of active). Activation to active rate prorated at $45,000/month equivalent if exercised.
- APAC Warm-Standby: capacity to bring up 30% of peak within 10 minutes — reservation fee = $7,500/month (25% of active).
- SLA + Failover credits: standard SLA applies; if activation is due to Redwood infrastructure failure, credit equals pro-rated downtime credit + one-month reservation fee applied as goodwill for first activation.

Option B (Lower initial cost):
- Pre-warm (on-demand) APAC with snapshot sync, no reserved APAC standby — lower monthly commitment; activation charges apply by token consumption.

We'd put these as an amendment to the renewal agreement (RDW-9876). We can start with Option A for the first 12 months, then re-evaluate at renewal.

Please confirm which option you'd like to pursue and any PO/payment terms. I can draft the amendment and circulate for legal redlines.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@medsilo.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire O'Neill <claire@medsilo.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby entitlement for renewal — procurement questions

Ben / Mina — thanks for the options. Procurement questions before we sign: 

1) PO & invoicing: MedSilo requires invoices to be monthly with net-30 payment and PO references. Will Redwood accept a single amendment with monthly invoicing?
2) Data residency & evidence: We need a recent SOC2 Type II snapshot and an audit log export format for the EU node (token-level logs for last 90 days) for our audit team. If the SOC2 report is not shareable, we need a secure link or SOC2 bridge letter.
3) DocuSign: we prefer DocuSign for the amendment. Can you provide a redline-ready PDF by EOD Mon 9/27?

Also: can you confirm the technical failover sequence (DNS cutover latency, KV sync approach, warm-up steps) so our SREs can validate the 10-minute target? We'll want to include a short runbook as an appendix.

Thanks — Tom Rivers
Procurement Manager, MedSilo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@medsilo.com>, Claire O'Neill <claire@medsilo.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby entitlement for renewal — next steps & test plan

Tom / Claire — appreciate the detail. Action plan from Redwood: 

- Commercial: Ben will produce a redline-ready amendment (PDF + DocuSign flow) by Mon 9/27. It will include Option A pricing and monthly invoicing with net-30.
- Security/artifacts: Priyom (cc) will provide a SOC2 Type II snapshot or secure access link and an example audit-log export format for the EU node; expect delivery by Tue 9/28.
- Technical failover plan: Engineering proposes a 3-stage failover: 1) traffic reroute via weighted DNS (target ~60–90s DNS TTL), 2) KV write-forwarding switch (stateful handoff ~3–5 min), 3) capacity spin from warm-standby to active (goal: <10 minutes).

I've attached a short failover checklist we'll use for the first drill (failover_test_checklist.md). Please confirm an approved test window (we propose Fri 10/8 02:00–03:30 UTC).

Once we have your confirmation on Option A and the PO/payment flow, Ben will circulate the DocuSign packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
